questions.question: When a fuel undergoes combustion, what is the primary way energy is transferred to the environment?
options: By cooling the surrounding air
By heating its surroundings
By absorbing light from the environment
By creating new mass in the container

questions.question: In a school laboratory, how can a student compare the amount of energy transferred by different burning fuels?
options: By measuring the volume of gas produced in a syringe
By heating a fixed amount of water in a boiling tube
By weighing the ashes left behind on a balance
By checking the color of the flame with a spectroscope

questions.question: To ensure a fair comparison of energy released by different fuels, which variable regarding the fuel must be kept constant?
options: The starting temperature of the fuel
The volume of the fuel container
The mass of fuel used in each test
The chemical formula of the fuel

questions.question: When comparing the energy output of different fuels by heating water, what must be kept the same for the water at the start of each test?
options: Only its chemical purity and pH level
Both its starting temperature and its volume
The material of the beaker and its depth
The rate at which the water is stirred

questions.question: How do state changes appear when analyzing a cooling curve graph of a substance?
options: As sharp, vertical drops in temperature
As flat, horizontal plateaus on the curve
As a continuous, steady diagonal line
As a series of random upward spikes

questions.question: What occurs as a gas or liquid cools down and transfers energy to its surroundings?
options: It may condense or freeze
It always increases its internal temperature
It will sublimate into a gas
It absorbs thermal energy from the air

questions.question: If a chemical reaction is described as exothermic, what observable change occurs in the surroundings?
options: The temperature of the surroundings decreases
The surroundings turn into a solid state
The temperature of the surroundings increases
The surrounding air pressure drops instantly

questions.question: What is the characteristic temperature change of the surroundings during an endothermic chemical reaction?
options: The temperature remains exactly the same
The temperature decreases
The temperature rises rapidly
The temperature fluctuates up and down randomly

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the energy transfer in an exothermic reaction?
options: Energy is transferred from the surroundings to the reactants
Energy is destroyed as the products form
Energy is transferred from the reactants to the surroundings
Energy is created within the nucleus of the atoms

questions.question: During an endothermic reaction, where is the energy transferred?
options: From the surroundings to the products
From the products to the reactants
From the reactants to the surroundings
From the container directly to the air

questions.question: Which of the following groups of state changes are all classified as endothermic processes?
options: Condensing, freezing, and melting
Melting, evaporation, and boiling
Freezing, boiling, and condensing
Sublimation, condensing, and freezing

questions.question: Why are condensing and freezing classified as exothermic processes?
options: They absorb heat from the surroundings to break bonds
They transfer energy out to the surroundings
They increase the temperature of the substance being cooled
They require an electrical spark to initiate

questions.question: Where does over half of the electricity in the UK come from?
options: Nuclear power plants and imported coal
The Sun, wind, and falling water
Burning natural gas and domestic wood
Geothermal energy and tidal barrages alone

questions.question: Which fossil fuel is no longer used to generate electricity in UK power stations?
options: Natural gas
Oil
Coal
Biomass

questions.question: Which of the following technologies produces electricity without using an electric generator?
options: Wind turbines
Hydroelectric dams
Solar panels
Biomass power stations
